headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading-error if oh-my-openagent feeds taipy outputs into shared workflows; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: oh-my-openagent can ingest browser content, files, and runtime-injected MCP/tool outputs; taipy is a data-engineering app that can produce workflow artifacts. No shared channel is documented, so direct hijack is unproven, but if taipy outputs are copied into agent_a’s prompts or files, agent_a may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions.
conditions: IF taipy outputs are pasted into oh-my-openagent prompts or AGENTS.md/README.md files
IF a shared MCP server or filesystem bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of taipy-generated text into agent_a prompts
Restrict agent_a MCP servers to trusted, provenance-tagged sources
Use a separate workspace directory for taipy artifacts
Add a prompt-injection scanner to taipy outputs before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce content provenance labels across the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches provider auth data, session history, and project code, while agent_b shows no data classes or network egress. With no shared workspace or upload path documented, leakage is not established; the main risk appears only if operator moves sensitive files from agent_a into taipy inputs or logs.
conditions: IF agent_a session history or provider auth data is exported into taipy datasets
IF both agents are pointed at the same directory containing secrets
mitigations: Keep agent_a auth files outside taipy input paths
Use separate OS users or directories for each agent
Redact session history before importing into taipy
Turn off verbose logging for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning on taipy ingestion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has broad network egress, browser, and subprocess capabilities; agent_b has no documented egress and no write surfaces. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so direct write contention is not evidenced. Uncertainty remains because agent_b’s I/O surfaces are empty rather than explicitly read-only.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same project directory or database
IF taipy is extended with external connectors that mutate shared state
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same git branch
Serialize any shared-state updates manually
Document ownership of mutable resources
requires-engineering: add locking around shared stores

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate browser-sourced or tool-sourced content, and taipy can consume data-engineering inputs or drive workflows. If taipy treats agent_a output as authoritative without validation, errors can cascade into downstream datasets or scheduled jobs. No verification layer is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF taipy ingests agent_a output as a dataset, config, or task definition
IF downstream Taipy workflows execute without human review
mitigations: Require schema validation on agent_a outputs before taipy ingestion
Add a human approval step for taipy job launches
Compare agent_a claims against source documents
Limit taipy to read-only consumption of agent_a outputs
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles provider auth prompts and session history, which may include regulated or sensitive operational data; agent_b’s profile shows no touched data classes or residency constraints. Because no explicit compliance mismatch is documented, the risk is limited to accidental policy drift if sensitive agent_a data is imported into taipy logs or datasets.
conditions: IF sensitive agent_a data is stored in taipy datasets or logs
IF taipy is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime different from agent_a’s operational policy
mitigations: Exclude auth prompts from taipy inputs
Set short retention on any shared logs
Review data-class labels before export
Keep sensitive artifacts in a separate region/account
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls
